blocks.text: Quick verdict

Decodo is the better all-round scraping provider: its pool is advertised at nearly four times ProxyEmpire's size, independent tests put its success rate near 99.9%, and it publishes clear prices up to 100 GB ($275). ProxyEmpire is the better fit if your traffic varies month to month, because its prepaid bandwidth never expires while Decodo's plan traffic resets, and if you want mobile and residential IPs under one account with ISP targeting included. For Google-heavy SERP work, Decodo is the safer choice.

Decodo and ProxyEmpire sit close together in the mid-market and price their entry gigabyte almost identically. The real differences are underneath: Decodo has a much larger advertised pool and scraping APIs for when raw proxies are not enough, while ProxyEmpire lets every prepaid gigabyte roll over indefinitely and includes ISP targeting and a combined residential-plus-mobile trial. If you are choosing a primary provider for scraping or account work, those structural differences matter more than a few cents per gigabyte.

blocks.text: Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo is the 2024 rebrand of Smartproxy, one of the most popular mid-market providers. Its residential network is advertised at 115 million IPs across 195+ locations, and independent benchmarks put its success rate around 99.9% with sub-second response times. Every plan includes the full pool plus city, state, ZIP and ASN targeting, and the dashboard is one of the easiest to set up. Decodo also sells datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies and a family of scraping APIs.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
ProxyEmpire in 2026: what you get

ProxyEmpire is a Bulgarian-registered provider (SWIFT SAAS LTD) that has been selling since 2020. Its residential and mobile networks share one system with 30M+ advertised IPs in 170+ countries, and country, region, city and ISP targeting are included at no extra cost. The standout policy is bandwidth rollover: prepaid traffic carries forward indefinitely, even after a subscription lapses. Proxyway's 2026 market tests found ProxyEmpire's pool was the third largest among the providers it tested.

Strengths: Prepaid traffic rolls over indefinitely; ISP/ASN targeting included at no extra cost; Cheap $1.97 trial covering residential and mobile; Unlimited residential option priced per day. Weak spots: Smaller advertised pool than the big three; Exact GB thresholds for each tier only shown at checkout; Weaker results on Google in some independent tests.
Pricing: Decodo vs ProxyEmpire

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

ProxyEmpire's rotating residential pricing currently starts at $3.50/GB (shown as 50% off a $7 list price) and steps down through several tiers to $1.50/GB at 1 TB, with custom pricing from about $0.75/GB above 5 TB. Rotating mobile starts at $4.50/GB, rotating datacenter at about $0.65/GB, and a flat-rate unlimited residential plan is sold by the day.

For 10 GB, there is little to separate them on price ($35 for Decodo, $35 for ProxyEmpire). At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because ProxyEmpire does not publish an exact price for that volume; Decodo comes to about $275. Look past the per-GB figure too. ProxyEmpire lets unused traffic carry forward, while Decodo's allowance does not (plan traffic resets monthly; payg for bursty work). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

By advertised size, Decodo (115M+) is about 3.8x larger than ProxyEmpire (30M+). Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Decodo lists 195+ countries and ProxyEmpire lists 170+. On targeting, Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while ProxyEmpire offers country, region, city and ISP/ASN (included by default).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration, and ProxyEmpire offers rotating or sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. How ProxyEmpire compares: stable connections and traffic that never expires.
SERP and rank tracking: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. How ProxyEmpire compares: Google was its weakest target in independent tests.

Social media and multi-account management: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Decodo: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard. ProxyEmpire: residential and mobile IPs with 24-hour sticky sessions. Let price and the countries you need decide.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Decodo: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. ProxyEmpire: free city and ISP targeting. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Ad verification and geo-testing: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Decodo: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. ProxyEmpire: ISP-level targeting at no extra cost. Let price and the countries you need decide.
Tight budgets: ProxyEmpire wins. The deciding factor for ProxyEmpire: rollover means nothing you pay for is wasted. The limitation on the Decodo side: it is mid-priced, not cheap.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile. Verification and payment rules differ too. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. ProxyEmpire: Standard verification. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Decodo and ProxyEmpire before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Decodo and ProxyEmpire is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential; ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile).

2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day. 3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Decodo comes out ahead in 2, ProxyEmpire in 1, and 3 are ties. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams, while ProxyEmpire is strongest for teams that hate losing unused bandwidth. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
